newsitem.title: USA: NYC mayor wants more state aid for tax cuts--paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC mayor wants more state aid for tax cuts--paper.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said his new budget plan will include tax cuts for city residents that total $47 million in 1998 and rise to $700 million a year by 2001, the New York Times reported Wednesday.
The package of cuts includes cuts in the city's income tax and the property tax for co-ops and condominiums, and a tax credit intended to encourage people on welfare to find jobs.
The paper said the plan faces many hurdles because the Republican mayor wants increased state aid to make up for the lost revenue from the proposed cuts.

The Republicans who control the state Senate, for example, reacted coolly to the package, saying they doubted they could agree to increasing aid to the city to the level the mayor would need to lower taxes as much as he proposed.
